title: Geometrically connected source over a connected target implies geometric connectedness of the target
statement: Let $k$ be a field. Let $T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Assume that $T$ is geometrically connected over $k$ and that $X$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

proof.text: Let $E/k$ be an arbitrary finite separable extension. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the singleton family $E/k$ to obtain a finite Galois extension $L/k$ and a $k$-embedding $E\hookrightarrow L$. Thus $L$ is also a field extension of $E$. Write $f:T\to X$ for the given $k$-morphism and $f_L:T_L\to X_L$ for its base change. We will first prove $X_L$ connected, then $X_E$ connected.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, finite Galois case; finite reduction through Tag 0389, lemma-characterize-geometrically-disconnected; Fields Tags 09DT and 0EXM (normal closure).

proof.text: By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $T_L$ is connected and nonempty. Its morphism $f_L$ makes $X_L$ nonempty. If $X_L$ were not connected, the definition [def-weil-connected-scheme] would give a partition $X_L=A\amalg B$ with both parts nonempty and clopen.

Apply [lem-trf-galois-connected-image-invariant-separation] to $f$, $L/k$ and that partition. The finite Galois and connected-source hypotheses hold by steps 1--2. Obtain a nontrivial clopen partition $X_L=P\amalg Q$ invariant under every $\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$.

Apply [lem-trf-galois-invariant-clopen-partition-descent] to $L/k$, $X$ and $P,Q$. Its hypotheses are exactly the invariance and partition assertions from step 3. The resulting partition $X=P_0\amalg Q_0$ has two nonempty clopen parts, contrary to connectedness of $X$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Thus $X_L$ is connected.

source.place: Tag 038C, lemma-tricky, invariant closed-set descent and contradiction.

proof.text: Let $\tau:E\to L$ be the $k$-embedding from step 1. Its spectrum map is a morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, because $\tau$ commutes with the structure maps. The induced map $q:X_L\to X_E$ is the cartesian base-change map of [def-pc-base-change]. The map $j$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective], so $q$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. A continuous surjection from the connected, nonempty $X_L$ makes $X_E$ connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]: its image is the whole target and the continuous image of a connected space is connected.

source.place: Tag 038C, finite Galois case; Morphisms Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective; connectedness descends by pulling back a partition.

proof.text: Since $E/k$ was arbitrary finite separable, apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-finite-separable-test] with $Y=X$. Step 5 verifies its right-hand condition; hence $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.

proof_origin.place: Tags 056R and 038C, finite Galois case, followed by the finite separable test of Tag 0389. Lean assembly uses the existing invariant-separation and clopen-partition-descent declarations; the final projection is baseChangeMap and its cartesian square is isPullback_baseChangeMap.
